full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No. 101 of 2001 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur against the defendant-respondent-petitioners and others for a declaration of title with a further declaration that the deed in the name of the defendants No. 29-32 is collusive, void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs along with a prayer for recovery of khash possession contending inter alia, that the suit properties appertaining to Mouza Ichli under Chandpur Sadar comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land out of 6.97 acres of land originally belonged to one Loknath and others. Subsequently, one Nurul Islam Sheikh in 12 annas and a Sekander Sheikh in 04 annas share obtained settlement from the original owners Loknath and others. During CS operation the suit land went under water and after its appearance from the bad of the river the Ex-Zaminder filed a Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 in which the settlement holders Nurul Islam and Sekandar obtained their respective saham. Thereafter, while Nurul Islam and Sekandar failed to pay the rent the Ex-Zamindar started a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 and in .Rent Execution Case No. 02 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain. Bhuiyan auction purchased the suit land by way of 'boynama' on 10-3-1951. The further case of the present petitioners i.e. the plaintiffs is such that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs namely Mohammad Ali and others by a registered sub-kabala deed dated 21-12-1956 became the owner of the suit land. The auction purchaser Zamir Hossain exhausted his share after his transfer. Thereafter, the SA khatian No. 28 was correctly prepared in the name of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land measuring 3.60 acres. The father of the plaintiff had been owning and possessing the land-in-dispute and after his demise the land was inherited by the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs after erecting their homestead in the suit properties use to possess the same and also paying rent to the government regularly. Out of the total land 42 decimals was recorded in the name of the plaintiff during BS operation and 461/2 decimals went into the khash khatian of the government. It is the case of the plaintiff that the suit land is in the khash land of the government but taking advantage of that the defendants No. 29-32 and 33-36 collusively obtained settlement from the government by kabuliyat dated 22-5-2000. On 20-2-2001 all on a sudden the defendants No. 29-32 dispossessed the plaintiffs from the 'kW schedule land forcibly and erected huts therein. The plaintiffs to the suit thereafter learnt about the settlement of the defendants from the government and after getting certified copy of the kabuliyate on 11-6-2001 filed the original suit. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the appellate court below during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs to the suit during trial after adducing sufficient evidence proved their case that the original owners of the disputed properties were Loknath and others and from them one Nurul Islam Sheikh and Sekandar Sheikh in 12 annas and 04 annas share took settlement. The learned Advocate also submits that during CS operation although the land-in-dispute went under water but subsequently it was re-appeared by alleviation and the Ex-Zamindar pursuant to a Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 gave the land amicably in favour of their settlement holders Nur Islam and Sekandar Sk. and in fact the partition suit was ended in favour of the Plaintiff's-Predecessors Nur Islam and Sekandar. Subsequently, for arrear of rent a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 was started and in Decree Execution Case No. 2 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain Bhuiyan auction purchased the suit land on 10-3-1951 and from that Zamir Hossain; predecessors of the plaintiffs kabala purchased the land-in-dispute. The learned Advocate also submits that the Lower Appellate Court during deciding the merit of the appeal after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law allowed the appeal and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below. 

 11. On perusal of the case records; it transpires that the positive contention as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs was such that the land-in-dispute originally belonged to ex-Zamindars namely Loknath and others. From them one Nur Islam Sheikh in 12 annas and one Sekandar Sheikh in 04 annas share took settlement. It is an admitted position that during CS operation the land in dispute went under water of the river. With regard to this; it is the contention of the plaintiffs that while the land-in-dispute reappeared from the bad of the river the ex-Zamindar started a "Touzi Bontan" (Partition Suit) Suit being No. 65 of 1930 and in that suit the settlement holder Nur Islam and Sekandar Sheikh obtained their respective saham in respect of the suit properties. The further pleadings of the plaintiffs were such that the Zaminders for arrears of rent started a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 and obtained a decree. In decree Execution Case No. 2 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain Bhuiyan auction purchased the land by way of "Boynama" on 10-3-1951. From that auction purchaser the predecessors of the plaintiffs obtained the suit land. 

 14. PW 1 is the plaintiff No. 5 himself namely Abdul Hamid Bepari. This witness in his examination-in-chief frankly conceded at a stage that during the CS operation the land-in dispute went under water and subsequently when the land reappeared the ex-Zamindar started a Partition Suit in which the earlier settlement holders of the Zaminders namely Nur Islam and Sekander Sheikh obtained a separate saham in respect of the suit properties. The plaintiff No. 5 in his testimony testified at a stage that during BS operation the land measuring 461/2 decimals become the khash land of the government in its khash khatian No.1. In his cross-examination he testified at a stage that they did not submit any paper showing the existence of the Partition Suit No. 65 of 1930 and also did not produce the judgment and decree passed in Rent Suit No. 350 of 1950. The plaintiff also admitted that they could not furnish any paper showing the existence of decree of the Execution case. At a stage of his testimony P.W.1 testifies that they did not sought for any relief against the government with regard to SA khatian which stands recorded in the name of government. He expressed his inability to state the CS khatian of the disputed property and also expressed his inability to state about the area of land in CS plot No. 251.
